text:
Lina: FYI rolled kernel canary 6.4.12 into eu-west-2 at ~02:10Z, seeing inconsistent peer access on a subset of Ampere racks (amp-ew2-rk04 rk05 rk07 rk08 rk09 rk10). NVLINK shows up but P2P sometimes fails or falls back to PCIe causing NCCL slow tails.

Kevin: Which exact racks and measurable impact?

Lina: Affected: rk04 rk05 rk07 rk08 rk09 rk10 (rk06 seems fine). Impact: multi-GPU jobs see 2-3x tail latency when P2P falls back; several NCCL jobs hit timeouts and restart. Rough calc: ~12% effective capacity reduction in EW2 training pool. If we move workloads to other regions expect short-term cost increase on the order of $5k-7k/month.

Ryan: Paste logs/topology you observed so we can determine kernel vs driver.

Lina: Snippets below:

```
# nvidia-smi topo -m (trimmed)
        GPU0    GPU1    CPU Affinity
GPU0    NV1     PX      0-23
GPU1    PX      NV1     0-23

# dmesg lines
[   43.123456] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: peer access failed: BAR1 mapping error
[   43.123789] nvidia 0000:66:00.0: peer access disabled by kernel: BAR1 allocation failed
[   43.124001] pci 0000:65:00.0: irq 43 for MSI
```

Also observed lspci showing ACS capability zero on some nodes:

```
0000:65:00.0 Display controller: NVIDIA Corporation A100-PCIE-40GB (rev a1)
	Capabilities: [100 v1] Advanced Error Reporting
	Capabilities: [14] PCI Advanced Features: ACS=0x0
```

Maya: So ACS bits differ between working and failing hosts. Did we push any firmware/BIOS changes with the canary?

Lina: No BIOS changes. Only kernel 6.4.12. My working theory: kernel changed PCI BAR allocation / IOMMU ordering and nodes with tight BAR1 windows fail to map peer BAR1 regions, so kernel disables peer access. Driver still at 525.89.

Kevin: OK. Proposed mitigations?

Lina: Short-term actions we can take now:
- Cordon and label affected nodes: kubectl label node amp-ew2-rk0{4,5,7,8,9,10} ampere.no-p2p=true and taint to prevent scheduling p2p-sensitive pods.
- Evict or reschedule multi-GPU jobs off the affected racks to unaffected racks or fallback dedicated pool.
- For tolerant workloads set NCCL_AGGREGATE_STATS=0 and NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 to avoid hard hangs.
- Roll back kernel canary on two racks as a quick test to validate hypothesis.

Ryan: Can we rollback a couple of racks now and watch if peer access returns?

Lina: Rolling back rk04 and rk08 now. Deploy-bot queued rollback jobs.

Deploy-Bot: kernel-canary rollback started for amp-ew2-rk04 at 2025-10-12T02:34Z by Lina

Infra-Bot: Telemetry alert: P2P fallback events spiked 02:12-02:22 on amp-ew2 (~1500 events/min peak).

Maya: If rollback restores P2P, hold the rest of the canary and open an SR with the kernel vendor and NVIDIA. If not, we'll audit BIOS/firmware and spin up a CI reproducer in-metal.

Lina: Initial rollback results: rk04 rollback completed and peer access re-enabled on 3/4 GPUs within 5 minutes. Ran a 4-GPU NCCL validation job and perf returned to ~baseline (no long tails). rk08 still finishing.

Kevin: Pause the canary rollout across EW2 and add scheduling filters to avoid placing multi-GPU pods on affected racks.

Lina: Paused canary via deploy-bot and applied ampere.no-p2p labels + taints to affected nodes. Created runbook in internal ops doc (link posted to SREs).

Ryan: We should surface the potential capacity/cost impact to finance: if this lasts >1 week and we shift significant training load to other regions we will hit higher commit tiers.

Kevin: @MTopS FYI: estimated temporary capacity shift EW2->other regions ~+$5k-7k/mo for ~2 weeks if sustained.

Maya: Next steps assigned:
- Lina: finish rk08 rollback, run nccl-test harness and paste logs.
- Lina/Ryan: repro in-metal with kernel 6.4.12 and capture PCI allocation traces.
- Kevin: open vendor SR with kernel dmesg, ACS evidence, and topo output.
- SREs: update scheduler filters and oncall runbook.

Lina: Will update this thread when rk08 rollback completes and attach nccl-test output.

Maria: Tagging for postmortem; add timeline and exact impact numbers once telemetry is aggregated.

Lina: rk08 rollback completed at 02:51Z, peer access restored and nccl-test passed 10/10. Blocking further canary hosts pending vendor response.

Kevin: Thanks all. Good escalation and clear runbook. :thumbsup:
